messages:
Avery: FYI apac-edge reported ~30% of new GPU nodes failing to join since 10:05 UTC, looks like bootstrap decryption failures
Rex: seeing the same, kubelet init logs: 
Rex: ```
2026-03-22T10:06:12Z ERROR decrypt token: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:apac:111222333:key/xxxx
```
Nora: we rolled a keystore policy update last night that tightened source IP constraints for keystore:Get*/Decrypt — ephemeral provisioning NAT ranges probably not included
infra-bot: alert: apac-edge node.join.failures > 25% (10m)
Avery: immediate mitigation options? we need nodes to register or we'll hit serving capacity issues and restart storms
Rex: quick fix: add warmpool NAT CIDRs to the policy allowlist temporarily and schedule an automated revert in 45m
security-bot: recommended: tag the change with `incident=apac-keystore-2026-03-22`, create an audit entry, and limit scope to the single bootstrap key and kms:Decrypt only
Nora: deployed a narrow patch to include provisioning NATs and `kms:ViaService` restriction at 10:12 UTC, will monitor
infra-bot: deploy-bot: keystore-policy patch applied to prod-canary at 10:12 UTC
Rex: join failures dropped to ~4% within 7m. autoscaler stabilized, warmpool drained safely
Avery: cost note: estimated extra ephemeral spend avoided ~ $9k by patching within 20m rather than waiting 4h
Nora: follow-ups: 1) replace IpAddress condition with `aws:SourceVpc` or `aws:SourceVpcArn` to be resilient to NAT churn, 2) add a staging canary that simulates ephemeral NAT churn during bootstrap, 3) update runbook to include this class of IAM failure
security-bot: will open a compliance ticket and schedule 1h post-incident review; will also prep audit diff for the temporary exception
Avery: thanks team — closing live ops thread, please add timeline + costs to postmortem and assign owners for policy rewrite and canary tests :thumbsup:
